title: SolarEdge Debuts U.S.-Made Duo Power Optimizer for Commercial and Industrial Projects, Delivering Module-Level Performance with 50% Fewer Units
summary: A 2:1 architecture with two independent MPPTs, connector-level safety monitoring, and industry-first arc fault detection with every optimizer acting as an arc sensor; open for U.S. orders now and on display at RE+ 2026 MILPITAS, Calif. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 2026-- SolarEdge Technologies, Inc.
body_markdown:
*A 2:1 architecture with two independent MPPTs, connector-level safety monitoring, and industry-first arc fault detection with every optimizer acting as an arc sensor; open for U.S. orders now and on display at RE+ 2026*


MILPITAS, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 2026-- SolarEdge Technologies, Inc. (Nasdaq: SEDG) today unveiled the new[SolarEdge Duo Power Optimizer](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.solaredge.com%2Fus%2Fproducts%2Fcommercial%2Fsolaredge-duo-power-optimizer-for-c-and-i&esheet=54641856&newsitemid=20261116795373&lan=en-US&anchor=SolarEdge+Duo+Power+Optimizer&index=1&md5=c87e9468248878d0e2332f64043d8767) for commercial and industrial (C&I) solar installations in the United States **,** building on its leadership in the commercial market. **1** The Duo delivers the same module-level energy harvest as a one-to-one power optimizer with half as many units to specify, wire and install, connecting two modules to one optimizer with an independent maximum power point tracker (MPPT) for each. It also features SolarEdge’s innovative Arc Fault Detection, a global industry first that uses every optimizer as an arc sensor to detect arcs at the source rather than only at the inverter.


This press release features multimedia. View the full release here:[https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116795373/en/](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116795373/en/)


U.S.-Made SolarEdge Duo Power Optimizer delivers Module-Level Performance with 50% Fewer Units


In a traditional string inverter system, the weakest module drags the output of the entire string, and the gap widens as modules degrade at different rates. With optimizers, an underperforming module affects only its own output.


“The bottom line is true module-level energy harvesting and visibility, with fewer optimizers to buy, wire and install,” said Gokul Krishnan, SVP and General Manager, North America at SolarEdge. “We also added safety features no one else in the industry has, including arc fault detection at the optimizer level. That addresses blind spots in the array where traditional string inverters can’t detect an arc. And the way we’ve designed the inputs gives installers real improvements in wire management on site.”


The Duo extends Sense Connect technology to every input and output connector, monitoring temperature to flag developing faults before an overheating connector can lead to an arc. With every Power Optimizer acting as an individual arc sensor, detection is distributed across the array instead of relying on a single point at the inverter, so if one optimizer misses an arc, its neighbor can catch it. Detecting close to where an arc can form enhances accuracy and sensitivity, helping stop an arc before it escalates. Protection covers strings with up to 3,280 feet (1,000 meters) of total cable length between the inverter and optimizer, and issues are pinpointed down to the optimizer area for quick, cost-effective resolution.


Each optimizer has two input pairs: a short pair for the closest module and a pre-extended pair for the adjacent one, reducing wire slack and eliminating field-made jumpers. Because one optimizer can connect two modules facing different azimuth angles, the Duo suits dual-tilt racking.


Manufactured in Florida, the Duo is designed to meet U.S. Domestic Content and FEOC requirements2 and is expected to ship to international markets in 2027. A single SKU covers commonly available modules, simplifying ordering for distributors and installers.


"We saw a clear difference in wire management on the roof, with fewer connections to make and no extra jumpers to run, which saved our crews real time during installation,” said Aaron Wilson, CEO of Solar One. “SolarEdge did an excellent job with the extension lengths, leaving very little excess wiring for our crews to manage. With the Duo, installers get module-level visibility with 50% fewer optimizers than one-to-one designs like the C651U. Being able to monitor performance down to the individual module gives us greater confidence in the system’s long-term output and makes troubleshooting far more precise when we do need to return to the site.”


The Duo Power Optimizer is available to order now in the U.S. through SolarEdge sales channels and distribution partners, with shipments expected to begin in January 2027. See it at RE+ 2026, November 17-19 in Las Vegas, booth N1516.


**About SolarEdge**

SolarEdge developed an intelligent inverter solution that changed the way power is harvested and managed in photovoltaic (PV) systems.
